title: Amazon Increases 2026 Capex to $220 Billion
description: Amazon has increased its capital expenditure for 2026 to $220 billion due to higher memory costs, according to CNBC.

sources.title: Amazon hikes 2026 capex to $220 billion due to higher memory costs

sections.heading: Amazon's Capex Increase
paragraphs: Amazon has announced an increase in its capital expenditure (capex) for 2026 to $220 billion, as reported by CNBC. This decision has been attributed to the rising costs of memory.

sections.heading: Reason for Increase
paragraphs: The increase in capex is primarily due to higher memory costs, which have impacted Amazon's spending plans for the year, as stated in the CNBC report.

sections.heading: Amazon's AI Infrastructure Spending
paragraphs: The Financial Times also reported on Amazon's increased spending, highlighting the company's commitment to bolstering its AI infrastructure.

sections.heading: Second Quarter Results
paragraphs: Amazon Investor Relations has announced the company's second quarter results, which provide further insight into Amazon's financial performance and strategic investments.

faq.a: Capex, or capital expenditure, refers to funds used by a company to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets such as property, industrial buildings, or equipment.

faq.q: Why has Amazon increased its capex?
faq.a: According to CNBC, Amazon has increased its capex for 2026 due to higher memory costs.

faq.q: How much has Amazon increased its capex?
faq.a: Amazon has increased its capex to $220 billion for the year 2026, as reported by CNBC.
